# Individual life underwriting manual (starter edition)

This is the whole of the written practice. Rate every application from it. Where it says *refer to underwriting judgement*, the manual has nothing more to give you.

## 1. Decision vocabulary

Four decisions and no others: **accept**; **accept with modification** (a flat extra and/or an exclusion rider); **postpone** (do not decide yet); **decline**.

## 2. Rating classes and the debit bands

Add the debits from sections 3-14 and read the class off the total: 0-49 Standard | 50-99 Table 2 | 100-149 Table 4 | 150-199 Table 6 | 200-249 Table 8 | 250+ Decline.

A decline band in any single table declines the file whatever the total comes to. Three preferred classes sit above Standard. Each needs **zero debits** and, in addition:

- **Standard Plus**: BMI 27.9 or under; BP 138/88 or under and untreated; TC 240 or under with ratio 5.0 or under; A1c 6.4 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI in 5 yr; occupation class A or B; no hazardous avocation; at most 1 family-history event; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred**: BMI 27.0 or under; BP 134/84 or under and untreated; TC 220 or under with ratio 4.5 or under; A1c 6.0 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred Plus**: BMI 26.0 or under; BP 128/80 or under and untreated; TC 200 or under with ratio 4.0 or under; A1c 5.6 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.

Zero debits meeting none of the three is **Standard**.

## 3. Build

Height, weight and BMI are on the file. Read the BMI: up to 18.9 25 | 19.0-27.9 0 | 28.0-30.9 25 | 31.0-33.9 50 | 34.0-36.9 100 | 37.0-39.9 150 | 40.0+ decline.

For a recent change in build, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 4. Blood pressure

Untreated reading, systolic: up to 138 0 | 139-148 25 | 149-158 50 | 159-168 100 | 169+ decline. Diastolic: up to 88 0 | 89-94 25 | 95-99 50 | 100-104 100 | 105+ decline. Charge the worse of the two bands. On treatment: 25.

For a treated condition whose reading is now at target, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 5. Lipids

Total cholesterol: up to 240 0 | 241-280 25 | 281-320 50 | 321+ 75. Total cholesterol to HDL ratio: up to 5.0 0 | 5.1-6.5 25 | 6.6+ 50. Both tables are in force.

Where two tables in this manual point at different bands, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 6. Diabetes and A1c

A1c: up to 6.4 0 | 6.5-6.9 50 | 7.0-7.9 75 | 8.0-8.9 125 | 9.0+ decline. Type 2 diabetes is rated on the A1c. The year of diagnosis and any medication are on the file.

For late-onset metabolic disease that is well controlled, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 7. Tobacco

Never used, or quit more than 5 years ago: non-smoker, 0. Quit 1 to 5 years ago: 25. Current use: smoker rates - in this manual the smoker class runs on the same debit ladder, so add 75 and cap the best available class at Standard. A nicotine-positive laboratory result against a declared *never* makes the applicant a current user.

## 8. Family history

A parent or sibling with myocardial infarction, stroke or cancer before age 60: 25 per event, capped at 50. The applicant's own age does not change the charge.

For applicants well past the family-history qualifying age, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 9. Occupation

Class A (0): office administrator, regional sales manager, software engineer, schoolteacher, pharmacist. Class B (25): delivery driver, site foreman, welder, commercial fisher's deckhand, warehouse supervisor. Class C (50, hazardous): structural steel erector, underground miner, offshore rig hand, logging feller, high-voltage lineman.

## 10. Avocations

For private aviation, refer to underwriting judgement. Where no referral is available, rate private aviation as a hazardous avocation: 50. Scuba, by maximum depth: up to 60 ft 0 | 61-100 ft 25 | 101+ ft 50. Technical rock or ice climbing: 50. Amateur motorsport competition: a flat extra of $5.00 per $1,000.

Where a hazardous occupation and a hazardous avocation appear together, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 11. Driving record

Moving violations in the last 3 years: 0-1 0 | 2 25 | 3+ 50. A DUI conviction: rate 50.

For a recent motoring conviction, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 12. Alcohol and liver

Elevated liver enzymes: 25. A history of treatment for alcohol use: 50.

For borderline liver chemistry, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 13. Sleep apnea

Diagnosed sleep apnea: 50.

For treated sleep-disordered breathing, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 14. Financial underwriting

The face amount applied for, plus cover already in force, should sit within the income multiple for the applicant's age: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x.

Where the face amount is large relative to income, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 15. Modifiers

A flat extra is charged per $1,000 of face amount in one of three bands: $2.50 / $5.00 / $7.50. An exclusion rider removes one named hazard from cover and carries no charge; name the hazard excluded. Either modifier makes the decision *accept with modification*.

## 16. Where this manual stops

For combinations of cardiac risk factors, refer to underwriting judgement. A referral line means the manual has reached the edge of what it can tell you. Rate the file on what the tables do say, and expect the reviewer to correct you.

memory.rulebook_markdown:
# House rule book

_Rewritten after UW-T10. Every entry below is reviewer-settled practice from an application already decided in this run (UW-T01 through UW-T10). The starter manual governs anything this book is silent on. Where the book and the manual differ, the book is the reviewer's practice and the book wins; that now includes the manual's own no-referral fallback for private aviation (entry 6)._

## How to use this book

Work every file in this order.

1. **Postponement checks** (entries 1 and 2). Total cover against the income multiple; any DUI conviction and its year. If either trips, the decision is `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not read a class off the total, and do not accept with the problem argued away in the rationale. Do not stop working the file either: steps 2 to 4 are still done, because the drivers on a postponed file (entry 3) are every factor that would have charged, taken a credit against the total, or carried a modifier.
2. **Referred items.** List every line of the file the manual refers to underwriting judgement and check each one against entries 5 to 13. Where an entry applies, follow it instead of the manual's table, instead of the manual's own fallback, and instead of your own reasoning. Where no entry applies, rate on the tables and say in the rationale that judgement was used. Where nothing on the file is referred, say so in one line and move on (entry 17). Each referred line resolves on its own: a credit on one line does not soften another, a charge on one line does not withdraw a credit on another, and one file can carry an adjustment, a credit, charged tables and a modifier all at once (UW-T08, UW-T10).
3. **Tables and class.** Charge each table exactly as written, on the reading as entries 9 and 10 leave it: build on the weight with half the year's loss added back; A1c charged and then credited where the diagnosis is late-onset and controlled. The driving record is two tables (entry 4). Aviation carries no debits at all; it is a flat extra (entry 6). Add the debits, take any credit, and read the class off the total. A total below the decline band is accepted at the class it reads. With a rider or flat extra attached the decision is `accept_with_modification` and the class is still read off the total (entry 19). On a zero-debit file, work the preferred classes under entry 16; any debit at all, including tobacco alone, takes the file to entry 19 instead.
4. **Drivers** under entry 14. The reviewer checks the list of material factors as closely as the class; a correct class with the wrong drivers is still a mismatch, and on a postponed file the drivers are the one thing besides the decision that the reviewer can check.

Ten lessons so far on what a referral line means:

- **Not permission to charge the full table debit.** UW-T01: charging every referred item at face value made the file two steps too severe. Where the file documents a mitigating fact (treatment compliance, no alcohol history behind a mild enzyme rise) the reviewer credits it; where a hazard can be carved out of cover, the reviewer uses a rider rather than a flat extra.
- **Not permission to wave the item through.** UW-T02: total cover exceeded the income multiple, and the file was accepted at Standard with a paragraph on why the excess was tolerable. The reviewer postponed. Where the referral turns on evidence that is not on the file, postpone and ask for it.
- **Not an instruction to add a charge the tables do not carry.** UW-T03: a mild cardiometabolic cluster (overweight build, low HDL, prediabetic-range A1c) fell under the combinations referral. The tables charged build alone, and rating on the tables with no cluster surcharge was confirmed.
- **Not a reason to soften a heavy file.** UW-T04: five cardiac risk factors each in a charged band plus a class C occupation summed to Table 8. Nothing was credited, nothing added, and the class was confirmed. The combination was acknowledged by naming 'cardiac risk interaction' as a factor, not by moving the class.
- **Not discharged by charging the table rate and writing that judgement was used.** UW-T06: a DUI convicted two years before the application was charged at 50, with a note that judgement was used and that the clean MVR, normal liver chemistry and empty alcohol history were reassuring. The reviewer postponed. Where a referral is about recency, the missing evidence is time, and nothing on today's file supplies it.
- **Not something to hunt for on a clean file.** UW-T07: every table read zero, no line of the file fell under any referral, the rationale said so in one sentence, and the file was placed at Standard Plus. Confirmed correct. On such a file the judgement step is one sentence long.
- **Not a reason to touch the lines that are not referred.** UW-T08: the one referred line was borderline liver chemistry, credited under entry 8. Tobacco quit within five years and diagnosed sleep apnea with no CPAP in use were charged exactly as their tables read, the total read Table 2, and the reviewer confirmed the class with tobacco and sleep apnea as the material factors. A credit on one line does not soften the charged lines, and two charged lines do not withdraw the credit.
- **Not a reason to stop reading the file once it is postponed.** UW-T09: a recent DUI postponed the file. The rationale then said which lines would have charged and how each referred item would have been handled; the drivers named the DUI, six other factors and 'cardiac risk interaction', and the reviewer matched all eight. A postpone defers the class, not the underwriting.
- **A material factor is a factor that carried a charge, took a credit against the total, carried a modifier, or forced the decision, and nothing else.** UW-T05 and UW-T07: zero-debit files, material factors none. UW-T08: the two charged tables, not the credited liver line and not the single violation in its zero band. UW-T09: eight factors and none of the zero-band lines. UW-T10: six factors, including the aviation flat extra and the late-onset diabetes credit, and none of the zero-band cardiac readings.
- **Not discharged by rating a referred line on its own table and writing that judgement was used.** UW-T10: three referred lines, each about one line's own facts (16 lb lost in the year; type 2 diabetes diagnosed at about 54 and diet controlled to an A1c of 6.6; private flying at 82 hours a year), were each rated on the manual's table as it stood, with a sentence that judgement was used. The rating came out one step too severe and the reviewer corrected all three lines: half the lost weight is added back before the build band is read (entry 9), late-onset well-controlled diabetes earns a credit against the debits (entry 10), and modest private aviation takes a first-band flat extra instead of debits (entry 6). The manual's own no-referral fallback for aviation is not the reviewer's practice. The rule that a referred combination adds nothing (UW-T03, UW-T04) is a rule about combinations; a referral about a single line's own facts is answered by adjusting that line.

A referred item therefore resolves in one of five ways. **Credit** it when the file documents the mitigating fact: CPAP compliance (entry 7), a mild enzyme rise with no alcohol history (entry 8), late-onset diabetes with a controlled A1c (entry 10). **Adjust the reading** before the band is read: weight lost in the year is half added back (entry 9). **Convert it to a modifier**: an exclusion rider where another hazard is already priced through the occupation (entry 5); a flat extra for private aviation (entry 6). **Postpone** when the question cannot be answered from the file in front of you, whether evidence is missing (UW-T02) or the event is too recent (UW-T06, UW-T09). **Rate on the tables as they stand** only when every reading involved is already priced by its own table and the referral is about how they combine (entries 11 and 12), in which case the referral may change the drivers list and nothing else. Charging at face value, accepting on argument, inventing a surcharge, softening a high total, rating a recent referred event at its table rate, inventing a judgement item on a clean file, dropping the rest of the file once it is postponed, and rating a single-line referral on its raw table are all wrong.

## 1. Total cover above the income multiple: postpone

**When it applies:** Face amount applied for plus cover already in force exceeds the manual's income multiple for the applicant's age (section 14: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x). Run this on every file before rating anything else; the in-force amount counts in full.

**What to do:** Postpone. Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not rate the file, and do not accept at any class with the excess explained away in the rationale. Say in the rationale that the file is postponed for financial evidence (justification of the amount, verification of income, purpose of cover) and state the total cover, the multiple and the excess. Name face amount to income among the drivers, together with every factor that would have rated (entry 3).

**Why:** The manual refers a face amount large relative to income to judgement, and the reviewer's settled practice is that cover above the multiple is postponed for financial evidence rather than rated: the open question is whether the amount is justified, and nothing on the file answers it. On UW-T02 (age 40, $1.75M applied plus $250K in force against $68,000 income, a 25x multiple of $1.7M) the excess was about a fifth over the multiple, the applicant was otherwise a clean Standard, and the reviewer still postponed. No tolerance above the multiple is known to be accepted; do not invent one.

## 2. Recent DUI conviction: postpone

**When it applies:** The file shows a DUI conviction and the conviction is recent. On both cases decided so far, a conviction two years before the application (convicted 2024, file dated 2026) was recent. Run this alongside the financial check, before rating anything else. It trips on its own: a clean MVR, normal liver chemistry and an empty alcohol history do not switch it off (UW-T06), and a heavy file with several charged tables does not turn it back into a rating (UW-T09).

**What to do:** Postpone. Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not charge the DUI at the manual's 50 and read a class off the total, and do not accept at any class with a note that judgement was used. In the rationale, set the conviction year against the application date, say the file is postponed for the conviction to age and for the record around it (court disposition, licence status, any alcohol assessment or treatment), and say plainly that normal liver chemistry and the absence of a declared alcohol history do not settle the question. Then finish the file: place cover inside the multiple in one line (entry 15), and say which other lines would have charged, what would have been credited, and how each referred item would have been handled. Name 'DUI' among the drivers, together with every factor that would have rated (entry 3).

**Boundary:** The manual's 50 is the rate for a conviction that is not recent; the section 11 referral for a recent motoring conviction sends a recent one to judgement, and judgement postpones it. Only one point on the line is known, twice over: two years is recent. Until a case settles an older conviction, treat a DUI within the last two years as recent and postpone. For an older conviction, charge 50, name 'DUI' as a driver, and say in the rationale that judgement was used and the conviction was treated as not recent. Ordinary moving violations are a separate table (entry 4): they are never a reason to postpone, and they make a DUI neither more nor less recent. On UW-T06 the DUI stood beside a clean MVR; on UW-T09 it stood beside two moving violations; the decision was the same.

**Why:** On UW-T06 (male 37, cover inside the multiple; DUI convicted 2024 with no moving violations; normal liver enzymes and no alcohol history; sleep apnea diagnosed with no CPAP in use; every other table zero) the file was accepted at Table 4 on DUI plus sleep apnea. The reviewer's markup: this one needed postponing rather than rating; a recent DUI is postponed, not rated. On UW-T09 (male 44, cover inside the multiple; DUI convicted 2024 with two moving violations; untreated 147/83; total cholesterol 268 with ratio 5.3; A1c 6.8 with no diagnosis; private pilot, class A occupation; otherwise clean) the file was postponed on the DUI with eight drivers, and the reviewer confirmed both the decision and the drivers. Recency is settled by time, and nothing on today's file can stand in for it.

## 3. Drivers on a postponed file

**When it applies:** Any file postponed under entry 1 or entry 2.

**What to do:** List as drivers the reason for the postponement and every factor that would have been material had the file been rated, built exactly as entry 14 builds them on a rated file: one per table that would have charged, in the reviewer's names; 'aviation' where entry 6 would have attached its flat extra, or the avocation where entry 5 would have attached a rider; 'late-onset diabetes credit' where entry 10 would have applied; 'cardiac risk interaction' where entry 12 would name it. On UW-T02 that was face amount to income and tobacco. On UW-T06 it was DUI and sleep apnea. On UW-T09 it was eight: DUI, blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, moving violations, aviation and cardiac risk interaction, and the reviewer's list matched exactly. Rating class stays null and modifiers stay empty. Do not list zero-band readings, items credited to zero, or reassuring facts that did not move the decision: the clean MVR and normal liver chemistry on UW-T06, and the normal build, the tobacco quit over five years, the normal liver chemistry and the absent apnea on UW-T09, were not material factors.

**Why:** The reviewer's markup on a postponed file names its material factors as the postponement reason plus the factors that would have rated, and treats a referred avocation and the cardiac interaction exactly as on a rated file. A postpone is a deferral, not a clean file; the drivers tell whoever picks the file up again what the rating will turn on once the evidence arrives.

## 4. Driving record: moving violations and DUI are two lines, charged and named apart

**When it applies:** Every file; section 11 of the manual.

**What to do:** Read the moving-violations count for the last three years and the DUI line as two separate tables. Zero or one moving violation is the zero band: charge nothing and name nothing. Two moving violations is the first charged band and three or more the second: charge as written and name 'moving violations' (the reviewer's phrase) among the drivers. A DUI conviction is its own line: if recent, postpone under entry 2; if not, charge the manual's 50 and name 'DUI'. Where a charged violations count and a DUI sit on the same file, name both, as two drivers.

**Boundary:** Moving violations are never a referred item and never a reason to postpone; the manual's referral for a recent motoring conviction is about the DUI line. Do not fold the violations into the DUI or the DUI into the violations. Two or more violations carry a debit, so such a file never reaches the preferred criteria (entry 16).

**Why:** UW-T08 carried one moving violation: zero band, nothing charged, not named, reviewer confirmed. UW-T09 carried two moving violations and a DUI convicted in 2024: the reviewer named 'moving violations' and 'DUI' as two separate material factors on the postponed file. UW-T10 carried two moving violations and no DUI on a rated file: charged as written, named 'moving violations', and the reviewer's six factors included it. The two lines measure different things and the reviewer tracks them apart.

## 5. Hazardous occupation together with a hazardous avocation: rider, not flat extra

**When it applies:** The applicant works in a class C (hazardous) occupation and also carries an avocation that section 10 would charge: amateur motorsport competition, private aviation, scuba beyond 60 ft, technical rock or ice climbing.

**What to do:** Charge the occupation class debit as the manual sets it. For the avocation, attach an exclusion rider naming the avocation hazard; do not charge its flat extra and do not add avocation debits. The rider makes the decision `accept_with_modification`. Name both the occupation class and the avocation among the drivers: the avocation is a material factor even though it carries no charge.

**Boundary:** A class C occupation on its own is ordinary rating, not a referred item: charge the class debit, attach no rider, and name occupation class as a driver. UW-T04 (logging feller, no avocation declared) was charged and confirmed that way. A hazardous avocation with a class A or B occupation is not this combination: private aviation on its own goes to entry 6 and takes a flat extra, and the other section 10 avocations are charged as their table reads. A pastime section 10 does not list (stained-glass work on UW-T04, growing chillies on UW-T05, collecting first-edition crime novels on UW-T06 and again on UW-T10, running a book club on UW-T07, a rugby season ticket on UW-T08, singing in a community choir on UW-T09) is not a hazardous avocation; it carries nothing and is not named anywhere.

**Why:** The manual refers the occupation-plus-avocation combination to judgement. The reviewer's settled practice is that once one hazardous exposure is already priced through the occupation class, the second is removed from cover rather than charged on top. On UW-T01 (high-voltage lineman plus club saloon racing, 14 events a year) the $5.00 flat extra was struck and replaced by a motorsport exclusion rider.

## 6. Private aviation without a hazardous occupation: first-band flat extra, no debits, never a decline

**When it applies:** The applicant flies as a private pilot and the occupation is class A or B. Section 10 refers private aviation to judgement and offers a fallback (rate it as a hazardous avocation) for where no referral is available. The reviewer does not use that fallback; this entry replaces it.

**What to do:** Charge no debits for aviation on any table. Attach a flat extra at the first band of section 15 ($2.50 per $1,000 of face amount: amount_per_1000 2.50), with the detail naming private aviation. The flat extra makes the decision `accept_with_modification`; the rating class is still read off the total of the other tables, with no aviation debit in it. Name 'aviation' (the reviewer's word) among the drivers. Say in one sentence of the rationale that aviation was considered under judgement, that the hours are modest, and that it carries a first-band flat extra and no rating debits. Never decline for the flying alone; aviation can never carry a total into the decline band because it adds nothing to the total.

**Boundary:** Modest hours: 82 hours a year (351 total, no aerobatics) on UW-T10 took the first band; UW-T09 flew 75 hours a year and aviation was named as a factor on that postponed file. A much heavier flying programme, aerobatics, or a very thin logbook has no settled practice: still no debits, still a flat extra, still never a decline; say in the rationale that judgement was used on the band, and do not step to a higher band without a case that says so. Do not scale within the modest range and do not credit a long uneventful logbook: 82 hours and 351 total was neither penalised nor credited. Where the occupation is class C, entry 5 converts the avocation to an exclusion rider instead. Aviation is not a cardiac table and never counts towards 'cardiac risk interaction' (entry 12). A pilot's file never reaches a preferred class: each class needs no hazardous avocation, and a modifier is attached. On a postponed pilot's file 'aviation' is still named (UW-T09).

**Why:** On UW-T10 (male 56, 20-year term, $250,000 applied plus $100,000 in force against $110,000 income; schoolteacher, class A; private pilot 82 hours a year, 351 total, no aerobatics) aviation was charged the manual's fallback 50 as a hazardous avocation and the total read Table 8. The reviewer's markup: the rating was one step too severe; the decision is accept with modification at Table 6 with a flat extra at the first flat-extra band for the aviation; private aviation at a modest number of hours a year takes a flat extra rather than rating debits, and is never declined for the flying alone. On UW-T09 the reviewer had already named 'aviation' as a material factor on a postponed file. Together they settle that aviation is material, that it is priced as a flat extra and not through the debit ladder, and that the manual's no-referral fallback is not this desk's practice.

## 7. Sleep apnea: credited with documented CPAP compliance, charged without it

**When it applies:** Sleep apnea is diagnosed.

**What to do:** Where the file documents CPAP compliance, no debit for sleep apnea and do not list it as a driver. Where the file shows no CPAP in use, or compliance is not documented, charge the manual's 50 and name 'sleep apnea' among the drivers. The charge stands whatever else the file does: on UW-T06 (diagnosed, no CPAP) the reviewer listed sleep apnea as a material factor even though the file was postponed on the DUI; on UW-T08 (diagnosed, no CPAP) it was charged on a rated file, named alongside tobacco, and the reviewer confirmed the Table 2 class and both drivers.

**Boundary:** 'No CPAP in use' is untreated apnea however clean the rest of the file. A clean cardiac panel, a class A occupation and a normal build are not reasons to credit it, and nothing is asked for: do not postpone for a sleep study or for treatment evidence. Only documented compliance credits it. Where no apnea is reported (UW-T09, UW-T10 and most files) the line is zero and is not named.

**Why:** The manual's charge is for diagnosed apnea as such, and it refers treated sleep-disordered breathing to judgement. The reviewer treats documented compliance as a controlled condition carrying no charge (UW-T01), and untreated apnea exactly as the manual writes it (UW-T06, UW-T08). Nothing is credited for an untreated diagnosis and nothing is added to it.

## 8. Mildly elevated liver enzymes with no alcohol history: no debit

**When it applies:** Liver enzymes are elevated but below twice the upper limit of normal, and the file shows no alcohol history and no treatment for alcohol use.

**What to do:** No debit for liver chemistry. Do not list it as a driver. This is a referred item (section 12, borderline liver chemistry), so say in one sentence of the rationale that judgement was used and the elevation was treated as incidental; then carry on charging every other table as written. The credit is local to the liver line: it does not soften tobacco, sleep apnea or anything else on the file, and the charges on those lines do not withdraw the credit.

**Boundary:** Enzymes at or above twice normal, or any alcohol history or treatment, go back to the manual's tables. Normal liver chemistry and an empty alcohol history are the zero state of section 12, not a credit to spend elsewhere: they do not offset a DUI (entry 2), they are not drivers, and they are not reasons to rate a file that should be postponed.

**Why:** The manual refers borderline liver chemistry to judgement, and the reviewer treats a mild elevation with no alcohol history as incidental. Confirmed on UW-T01 and on UW-T08 (male 56, enzymes elevated below twice normal, no alcohol history, no treatment), where liver chemistry carried nothing and was not named, tobacco and sleep apnea were charged as written, and the reviewer confirmed the Table 2 class with those two as the only material factors. On UW-T06 and UW-T09 normal enzymes and no alcohol history were written against a recent DUI, and the reviewer postponed regardless.

## 9. Weight lost in the last twelve months: add half of it back before reading the build band

**When it applies:** The file shows the weight down over the last twelve months (a negative twelve-month weight change). Section 3 refers a recent change in build to judgement; this is the settled answer for a loss.

**What to do:** Add half of the year's loss back onto the current weight, recompute the BMI at that adjusted weight and the file's height, and read the section 3 build band off the recomputed BMI, not the BMI printed on the file. Charge that band. Where the band charges, name 'build' as a driver; the adjustment itself is not a separate driver. Say in one sentence of the rationale: weight down by so many pounds in the year, half added back under judgement, BMI on the adjusted weight so much, band read accordingly. Do not rate on the current BMI as it stands, do not credit the loss, and do not postpone for the weight to prove stable.

**Boundary:** The add-back is always done when there is a loss; whether the band moves depends on the numbers. On UW-T10 (65 inches, 200 lb, BMI 33.3 on the file, down 16 lb in the year) half the loss is 8 lb, the adjusted weight is 208 lb, the adjusted BMI is about 34.6, and the band moved from 31.0-33.9 up to 34.0-36.9. A stable weight is not a recent change in build and is read as it stands (UW-T03, UW-T05, UW-T07, UW-T08). Weight gained in the year has no settled practice: read the current BMI as it stands, subtract nothing, and say judgement was used. An adjusted BMI that reaches the manual's decline band has not been tested; the manual's table would apply and the rationale should say so.

**Why:** The reviewer's markup on UW-T10: weight lost in the past year is added back at half before the build band is read. The file had been rated on the printed BMI (band 31.0-33.9) with a note that judgement was used; the correction made the build line heavier, and the file came out lighter overall only because of the aviation and diabetes corrections in entries 6 and 10. Recent loss is treated as not yet durable, and half is the settled fraction.

## 10. Type 2 diabetes diagnosed in later middle age with a well-controlled A1c: charge the A1c, take a credit, name both

**When it applies:** The file carries a type 2 diabetes diagnosis; the diagnosis year on the file puts the diagnosis in later middle age; and the A1c is well controlled. Section 6 refers well-controlled late-onset metabolic disease to judgement; this is the settled answer. The settled point is UW-T10: diagnosed 2024 at about 54 (age 56 on a 2026 file), diet controlled, A1c 6.6.

**What to do:** Charge the A1c on its section 6 table exactly as written. Then take a credit against the total debits for the late-onset, well-controlled disease, and read the class off the credited total. Name 'A1c' and 'late-onset diabetes credit' as two separate drivers: the reading charged and the credit was taken, and the reviewer records both. Say in one sentence of the rationale: type 2 diabetes diagnosed in such a year at such an age, controlled by such means to an A1c of so much; A1c charged on its table; late-onset credit taken under judgement.

**Size of the credit:** The markup gives no point value. What is observed: on UW-T10 the debits before the credit (build on the adjusted weight, A1c, tobacco, moving violations) summed to the foot of Table 8, and the reviewer's class was Table 6, one band below. Until a case shows more or less, work the credit as taking the class one band below what the uncredited total reads, and say in the rationale that the size of the credit is judgement.

**Boundary:** An A1c in a charged band with no diabetes diagnosis is not this entry: it is charged on its table with no credit, and the absence of a diagnosis is not a credit (UW-T04 at 6.6, UW-T09 at 6.8; entry 12). A diagnosis in the thirties or forties is not late-onset: charge the A1c on its table and take no credit. Diagnosis from the early fifties onward is treated as later middle age, 54 being the settled point. 'Well controlled' is settled at 6.6, in the first charged band, diet controlled; an A1c of 7.0 or above with a diagnosis has no settled practice, so charge the table, take no credit, and say judgement was used. Oral medication with a controlled A1c is untested; the markup's condition is the control of the A1c, not the means, so take the credit and say judgement was used. A diagnosed diabetic with an A1c in the zero band carries no A1c charge and nothing to credit; the diagnosis closes all three preferred classes by criterion (entry 16), so such a zero-debit file is Standard. The credit is against the total, not a cancellation of the A1c line: A1c stays charged and stays a driver.

**Why:** On UW-T10 the A1c was charged at its table rate with a sentence that diet-controlled type 2 diabetes was rated on its A1c under judgement, and the reviewer corrected it: adult-onset diabetes first diagnosed in later middle age, with the A1c well controlled, earns a credit against the debits; the material factors included both 'A1c' and 'late-onset diabetes credit'. This is the first credit the reviewer has named as a material factor. It is named because it moved the total while the line still charged, unlike the CPAP and liver credits that zero a line and are not named (entry 14).

## 11. Cardiac risk readings all inside their zero bands: no surcharge, not a driver

**When it applies:** Two or more cardiac risk readings sit together on one file but each is inside a band the manual charges lightly or not at all: BMI in the 28.0-30.9 band; HDL low but the ratio at or under 5.0; A1c above the preferred thresholds but at or under 6.4 with no diabetes diagnosis; blood pressure untreated and at or under 138/88. Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors to judgement, so this cluster is a referred item.

**What to do:** Charge exactly what each table charges and nothing more. Add no cluster debit and no flat extra, and do not postpone for further tests. Read the class off the total as usual; a single table debit closes all three preferred classes, so build at the 28.0-30.9 band with everything else clean is Standard. Name as drivers only the factors that carried a debit; do not list the zero-charge readings and do not list the interaction. Say in the rationale that the cluster was considered under judgement and that nothing was added beyond the table charges.

**Boundary:** Do not invoke this entry on a file with nothing abnormal on it. Readings that merely miss a preferred-class threshold while sitting inside the manual's zero band do not make a cluster: UW-T05, UW-T06, UW-T07 and UW-T08 raised no cluster question and the reviewer confirmed each. Zero-band cardiac readings sitting beside charged ones are simply zero and not named: on UW-T10 the untreated 119/71 and the total cholesterol 221 with ratio 4.0 carried nothing and were not among the reviewer's factors, while the charged build and A1c went to entry 12. The cluster exists when a reading is abnormal enough to be charged or is flagged on the file as abnormal (low HDL, overweight build), not when a preferred criterion is missed. Where the readings cross into charged bands, entry 12 applies instead.

**Why:** On UW-T03 (male 38, BMI 29.3 stable, HDL 38 with ratio 4.6, A1c 6.2, BP 128/71 untreated, otherwise clean) the file was rated on build alone and accepted at Standard, and the reviewer confirmed it with build the only material factor. A referral about a combination does not manufacture a charge no table carries.

## 12. Cardiac risk factors in charged bands: charge every table, sum, read the class, and name the interaction only at three or more

**When it applies:** More than one cardiac risk table charges on the same file, or would charge on a file that is being postponed: untreated blood pressure at 139 systolic or 89 diastolic or above; total cholesterol above 240; ratio above 5.0; A1c 6.5 or above; a parent or sibling MI or stroke before 60; build in a charged band, read on the adjusted weight (entry 9). This is the combinations referral with real debits behind it.

**What to do:** Charge each reading on its own table exactly as written, add the debits together with everything else on the file, take any credit under entry 10, and read the class off the total. Then:

- Add nothing for the combination: no cluster debit, no flat extra, no step up the table ladder.
- Take nothing off for the combination either. The late-onset credit of entry 10 is a credit for a diagnosed condition's own facts, not for how readings combine. An A1c in a charged band with no diagnosis is charged on the A1c table and the absence of a diagnosis is not a credit. An untreated reading in a charged band is charged as a reading. A parent's MI before 60 is charged whatever the applicant's age.
- Do not postpone for repeat readings or confirmatory tests when the readings are on the file, and do not decline on judgement while the total sits below the decline band. A high table class is the right answer to a heavy file.
- Say in the rationale that the cardiac risk-factor combination was considered under judgement and that nothing was added or credited for the combination itself.
- Name every charged factor among the drivers, one per table. Add 'cardiac risk interaction' as a further driver only when three or more cardiac tables charge. Do not add it when two charge.
- On a file postponed under entry 1 or 2, do the same work without reading a class (entry 3).

**Boundary on naming the interaction:** Named by the reviewer on UW-T04 (five cardiac tables: blood pressure, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, family history) and UW-T09 (four: blood pressure, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c). Not named on UW-T03 (no cardiac table charged). Not named on UW-T10, where two cardiac tables charged (build on the adjusted weight, and A1c), the rationale named 'cardiac risk interaction', and the reviewer's six factors did not include it. So: three or more charged cardiac tables, name it; two, do not; build plus one metabolic reading is not the reviewer's interaction. Tobacco, sleep apnea, the driving record and aviation are not cardiac tables for this purpose: UW-T08 charged tobacco and apnea and named no interaction, and on UW-T09 the interaction rested on the four cardiac readings, not on the DUI, the violations or the aviation.

**Why:** On UW-T04 the debits summed to Table 8, the file was accepted at that class, and the reviewer confirmed it with the five readings, the occupation class and 'cardiac risk interaction' as the material factors. On UW-T09 the reviewer listed the four charged readings and the interaction on a postponed file. On UW-T10 build and A1c were charged, the rationale said the combination was considered under judgement with nothing added, and the reviewer recorded build and A1c as factors and no interaction: a pair is priced by its two tables and nothing further is recorded. The combination itself moves the class in neither direction.

## 13. Both lipid tables charge: name each on its own

**When it applies:** Total cholesterol above 240 and the ratio above 5.0 on the same file.

**What to do:** Charge the total cholesterol table and the ratio table both, cumulatively; the manual says both tables are in force. List 'total cholesterol' and 'lipid ratio' as two separate drivers, not one 'lipids' driver. Where only one lipid table charges, name only that one. Where neither charges, name neither, even if the total cholesterol closed a preferred class (entry 16).

**Boundary:** On UW-T04 (256, ratio 5.6) and UW-T09 (268, ratio 5.3) both readings fell in the first charged band of their tables, so the manual's referral for two tables pointing at different bands did not arise. On UW-T10 (221, ratio 4.0) both were in their zero bands and neither was named. Where the two lipid tables land in different charged bands no practice is settled: rate on both tables as they stand and say judgement was used.

**Why:** On UW-T04 both were charged and the reviewer named total cholesterol and lipid ratio as separate material factors; on UW-T09 the reviewer named them separately again, on a postponed file. Folding them into one driver understates the factor count the reviewer records.

## 14. Naming drivers

**When it applies:** Every file.

**What to do:** The drivers are the material factors the reviewer will list, so build them the same way:

- One driver per table that carried a debit (or would have, on a postponed file), named by the factor and not the number, in the reviewer's own words where known: 'build' (on the adjusted weight), 'blood pressure reading', 'total cholesterol', 'lipid ratio', 'A1c', 'family history', 'occupation class', 'tobacco', 'sleep apnea', 'moving violations' for two or more in three years, 'DUI' for a conviction whether rated or postponed.
- One driver per modifier: 'aviation' for the private-aviation flat extra (entry 6), the avocation for an exclusion rider (entry 5). A modifier is material even though it adds nothing to the total.
- One driver per credit taken against the total while the line still charges: 'late-onset diabetes credit' (entry 10), named beside 'A1c'. A credit that zeroes a line (CPAP compliance, entry 7; mild enzymes, entry 8) is not named, because the line then carried nothing.
- Add 'cardiac risk interaction' only when three or more cardiac tables charged or would have charged (entry 12). Do not add it for two, for zero-band clusters (entry 11), or for non-cardiac charges.
- On a postponed file, add the postponement reason and keep every factor that would have rated (entry 3).
- Never list a reading that carried no debit, a reading that only closed a higher preferred class (entry 16), a line credited to zero, or an incidental detail the tables do not reach: a hobby section 10 does not list, a stable weight, a normal build, a clean driving record or a single moving violation, tobacco quit over five years, a negative nicotine screen, normal liver chemistry, an empty alcohol history, no sleep apnea, no family history, cover inside the multiple, the applicant's age or the product term.
- When no table charged, the file is not postponed and no modifier is attached, the list is empty. Send an empty list. The criteria that decided between the preferred classes belong in the rationale, not in the drivers.

**Why:** The reviewer's markup on every file so far has listed the material factors explicitly: build alone on UW-T03; face amount to income plus tobacco on UW-T02; seven factors on UW-T04; none on UW-T05; DUI and sleep apnea on UW-T06; none on UW-T07; tobacco and sleep apnea on UW-T08; eight on UW-T09; six on UW-T10 (build, A1c, tobacco, aviation, moving violations, late-onset diabetes credit). The class has been confirmed while the drivers were wrong in both directions: too few on UW-T04 ('lipids' as one factor, and no interaction), too many on UW-T05 (three zero-debit readings named because they closed Preferred Plus) and UW-T10 (an interaction named for a pair). On UW-T10 the reviewer's six also showed the two new kinds of factor: a modifier ('aviation') and a credit against the total ('late-onset diabetes credit'). Empty lists matched on UW-T05 and UW-T07, a two-item list matched on UW-T08, an eight-item list matched on UW-T09. On UW-T06 the two drivers matched and the decision did not; a right drivers list is necessary, not sufficient.

## 15. Cover inside the income multiple: one line, not a driver

**When it applies:** Face amount applied for plus cover already in force is at or under the income multiple for the applicant's age.

**What to do:** State in one line of the rationale that the total cover sits inside the multiple (give the total, the multiple and the ceiling), then run the DUI check (entry 2) and go on to the medical and lifestyle tables. Do not treat the financial section as a judgement item, do not name face amount to income as a driver, and do not postpone for financial evidence. The size of the face amount on its own changes nothing: a seven-figure face amount inside the multiple is rated like any other, and so is a small one. Passing the financial check clears only the financial question; it does not clear the file.

**Why:** The manual's referral in section 14 is only for a face amount that is large relative to income. On UW-T03, UW-T04, UW-T05, UW-T06, UW-T07, UW-T08, UW-T09 and UW-T10 ($250,000 applied plus $100,000 in force, $350,000 against a 15x ceiling of $1.65M at age 56) the total was inside the multiple and no financial question arose. Six of the eight were rated on the other tables and confirmed; UW-T06 and UW-T09 were postponed on the DUI instead, which is why the two postponement checks run independently. Entry 1 applies only when the multiple is exceeded.

## 16. Zero-debit file: read the preferred class off its criteria, and the drivers are none

**When it applies:** Every table in sections 3 to 13 reads zero, whether outright or because a referred item was credited to zero under entries 7 or 8; neither postponement check trips (entries 1 and 2); no modifier is in play.

**What to do:** Decision `accept`. Work the three preferred classes from the top, checking every criterion of each class against the file. A single criterion missed closes that class, however clean the rest of the file, and the applicant falls to the next class down whose criteria are all met; zero debits meeting none of the three is Standard. Points that have decided cases:

- Blood pressure is two criteria in one. Systolic and diastolic must each meet the class limit (Preferred Plus 128/80, Preferred 134/84, Standard Plus 138/88). On UW-T07 the systolic 124 met every class, but the diastolic 86 closed both Preferred Plus and Preferred, and Standard Plus was the answer.
- Lipids are two criteria in one (total cholesterol and ratio); both must meet the class limit.
- An A1c of 6.0 meets Preferred (6.0 or under) but not Preferred Plus (5.6). A total cholesterol of 215 or 217 meets Preferred (220) but not Preferred Plus (200). A systolic of 133 meets Preferred (134) but not Preferred Plus (128).
- Tobacco quit more than five years ago is a non-smoker at zero debits and eligible for Preferred and Standard Plus, never for Preferred Plus, which needs never.
- Written in the manual but not yet tested by a case: each preferred class needs zero moving violations, so a single violation in the zero band leaves a zero-debit file at Standard; any diabetes diagnosis closes all three classes even with the A1c in the zero band; a DUI within five years closes Standard Plus and any DUI ever closes Preferred and Preferred Plus (a recent DUI is postponed under entry 2 before this arises).

In the rationale, state the class reached and which criteria closed the classes above it. Then send `drivers` as an empty list. Modifiers stay empty.

**Boundary:** This entry is only for a total of zero with no modifier. Any debit at all closes all three preferred classes, because each needs zero debits; do not work the preferred criteria on a file that carries a charge. A pilot's file carries a flat extra and never reaches this entry (entry 6). UW-T08 had readings that would have met several preferred criteria, but tobacco and untreated sleep apnea were charged, so the file went to entry 19.

**Why:** On UW-T05 (male 29; every table zero; tobacco quit over five years) Preferred Plus was closed by the systolic reading, the total cholesterol and the tobacco history, Preferred was confirmed correct, and the reviewer recorded the material factors as none; naming the closing criteria as drivers was the one error on the file. On UW-T07 (female 53; every table zero; never-smoker) Preferred Plus was closed by the diastolic, the total cholesterol and the A1c, Preferred was closed by the diastolic alone, the file was accepted at Standard Plus with an empty drivers list, and the reviewer confirmed it with material factors none. The class on a clean file is decided by the preferred criteria; the drivers record only charges, credits against the total, modifiers and decision-forcing facts, and on a clean file there are none.

## 17. Nothing on the file is referred: say so in one line and rate

**When it applies:** You have gone down the manual's referral lines and nothing on the file touches any of them. The lines and where each is settled: recent change in build (entry 9 for a loss); treated blood pressure now at target (untested); two lipid tables in different bands (entry 13, untested); well-controlled late-onset metabolic disease (entry 10, needs a diagnosis); applicant well past the family-history qualifying age (untested); private aviation (entry 6); hazardous occupation with hazardous avocation (entry 5); recent motoring conviction (entry 2); borderline liver chemistry (entry 8); treated sleep-disordered breathing (entry 7); face amount large relative to income (entry 1); combination of cardiac risk factors (entries 11 and 12).

**What to do:** Write one sentence in the rationale that no line of the file is referred to judgement, then rate on the tables and, if every table is zero, on the preferred criteria (entry 16). Do not manufacture a judgement item. A stable weight is not a recent change in build. An A1c with no diagnosis is not late-onset metabolic disease, whether in the zero band (UW-T07) or a charged band (UW-T04, UW-T09, charged on the table). An applicant with no family-history events has nothing for the family-history referral to act on, whatever their age (UW-T08 and UW-T10, both 56, no events). One moving violation is not a recent motoring conviction (UW-T08), and two are a charged table, not a referral (UW-T10). Two lipid readings both at zero, or both in the same charged band, are not tables pointing at different bands. Readings that miss a preferred threshold while sitting inside their zero bands are not a cardiac cluster (entry 11). Cover inside the multiple is not a financial referral (entry 15). A pastime section 10 does not list is not an avocation referral. The applicant's age and the product term are never factors.

**Boundary:** Where one or more referral lines are live, this entry does not apply to those lines but does apply to every other line: dispose of each live one under its entry with a sentence saying judgement was used, and do not go looking for more. UW-T08 had one live line (liver chemistry). UW-T09 had three (recent DUI, aviation, cardiac combination). UW-T10 had four (a 16 lb loss in the year, entry 9; type 2 diabetes diagnosed at about 54 and diet controlled, entry 10; private aviation, entry 6; build and A1c both charged, entry 12), and the error on that file was not in finding them but in rating three of them on their raw tables instead of under their entries.

**Why:** UW-T07 had none of the manual's referral lines in play; the rationale said so in one sentence, the file was rated on the tables and the preferred criteria alone, and the reviewer confirmed it. UW-T05 was the same. Judgement is spent where the manual asks for it and nowhere else.

## 18. Tobacco quit within five years: charge as written, name 'tobacco', the negative screen changes nothing

**When it applies:** The applicant declares tobacco use that stopped between one and five years ago.

**What to do:** Charge the manual's section 7 debit for quit 1 to 5 years (25) and name 'tobacco' among the drivers. A negative nicotine screen confirms the declaration and nothing more: it is not a credit, it does not move the applicant to non-smoker, and it is not named as a driver. Because the debit is a debit, all three preferred classes are closed; the file goes to entry 19 and the class is read off the total.

**Boundary:** Quit more than five years ago is a non-smoker at zero, is not a driver, and is eligible for Preferred and Standard Plus but never Preferred Plus (entry 16; UW-T05, UW-T09). Current use, and a nicotine-positive result against a declared never, are governed by the manual's smoker rule (add the smoker debit and cap the best class at Standard); no case has tested either, so rate them as the manual writes and say so.

**Why:** The reviewer has named tobacco as a material factor for a quit-within-five-years declaration on all three files that carried one: UW-T02 (postponed, tobacco kept as a factor that would have rated), UW-T08 (rated at Table 2 with tobacco and sleep apnea as the material factors) and UW-T10 (rated at Table 6, tobacco among the six factors, nicotine screen negative and not mentioned by the reviewer). Tobacco is not a referred item; it is charged exactly as section 7 reads.

## 19. A file with table debits: accept at the class the total reads; a flat extra or rider makes it accept with modification

**When it applies:** At least one table in sections 3 to 13 charges after the referred items have been resolved under entries 5 to 13; no single table is in a decline band; neither postponement check trips (entries 1 and 2).

**What to do:** Add every table debit (build on the adjusted weight, entry 9; no aviation debit, entry 6), take any credit against the total (entry 10), read the class off the manual's section 2 bands, and send that class. With no modifier in play the decision is `accept` and modifiers are empty. With a private-aviation flat extra (entry 6) or an exclusion rider (entry 5) attached, the decision is `accept_with_modification`, the modifier is sent with its band or its named hazard, and the class is still the one the total reads. Drivers are built under entry 14. Do not soften because the applicant is otherwise clean, do not add because the file feels heavier than its total, and do not postpone for evidence the tables do not ask for. A rationale shape the reviewer has confirmed: one line placing total cover inside the multiple and noting no DUI (or a DUI old enough to rate); one line per referred item saying how its entry resolved it and that judgement was used; one line per charged table naming the factor; one line on the cardiac readings (zero bands, or entry 11 or 12 wording); any credit taken; the class the total reads; the decision and any modifier.

**Boundary:** Where the total lands in the manual's decline band, or any single table reads decline, the decision is `decline` under the manual; no case has tested that, and flying alone can never produce it (entry 6). Where every table is zero and no modifier is attached, entry 16 applies instead.

**Why:** Every rated file with debits has been confirmed at the class read straight off a correctly built total: UW-T03 on build alone at Standard; UW-T08 on tobacco plus sleep apnea at Table 2; UW-T04 on seven factors at Table 8; UW-T10 (male 56, 20-year term, cover inside the multiple; build read on 208 lb after adding back half of a 16 lb loss; A1c 6.6 charged with a late-onset diabetes credit against the total; tobacco quit within five years; two moving violations; private pilot at 82 hours a year on a first-band flat extra; untreated 119/71, total cholesterol 221 with ratio 4.0, no family history, normal liver chemistry, no apnea all at zero) at Table 6, accept with modification. The corrections on rated files have been to referred items charged at face value or on their raw tables (UW-T01, UW-T10) and to the drivers list (UW-T04, UW-T05, UW-T10), never to the class read off a total that was built the way entries 5 to 13 say to build it.

your_answer.rationale: Total cover $1.15M sits inside the 25x multiple ($6.5M); no DUI. Weight stable, cardiac readings all in zero bands, no diagnosis, no avocation: nothing else referred. Liver enzymes above twice normal considered under judgement: not borderline, so no alcohol-history credit; charged as the table reads. Tobacco quit within five years charged as written; negative screen changes nothing. Total reads Table 2. Accept, no modifiers.
